newsitem.title: CANADA: Forest fires crimp Canada timber operations.
newsitem.headline: Forest fires crimp Canada timber operations.

text.p: Hundreds of forest fires raging across the northern parts of central Canada were putting a crimp in timber operations on Thursday as officials took precautionary measures against further outbreaks of fire.
Government officials in Quebec and Ontario said timber harvesting operations were halted or scaled back in those regions hardest hit by fires being fueled by hot, dry conditions and brisk winds.
Lumber industry representatives, however, said they did not expect producers to face immediate shortages of raw timber for processing into lumber.

"I think that a good part of our members would have a stockpile ranging anywhere from a week to three months," said Richard Hudon, chief inspector with the Canadian Lumbermen's Association, an Ottawa-based industry group.
Under Quebec and Ontario government regulations, authorities can order timber producers to cease operations entirely or for certain parts of the day to help prevent further fire outbreaks.

"They may allow the industry to operate at night or go into the bush at four o'clock in the morning to harvest and haul until 8 a.m." said Bob Thomas, spokesman for the Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources Provincial Response Centre in Sault-Saint-Marie.
Thomas said more than 60 forest fires were burning in Ontario, with the likelihood that lightning storms would start others in the coming days.
A thunderstorm in northern Ontario on Wedneday brought little relief in the form of precipitation but produced 4,000 recorded lightning strikes, Thomas said.
"Out of those 4,000 lightning strikes, we anticipate picking up in excess of 30 new firestarts a day for the next few days," he said.
Thomas said more than 39,535 acres (16,000 hectares) of forest area had already been lost to fire in Ontario.

One 17,300-acre (7,000-hectare) fire was burning in a busy cottage and resort area about 19 miles (30 km) southeast of the town of Timmins in northeastern Ontario. No injuries were reported as about 100 vacationers were displaced from the area.

In the neighboring French-speaking province of Quebec, 95 forest fires were reported, consuming an estimated 123,548 acres (50,000) hectares of timberland, officials said. More than 1,600 people were evacuated from two villages on Wednesday, and about 800 firefighters were battling the blazes on the ground.

In the Quebec region north of the St. Lawrence River, sawmills owned by Donohue Inc and privately-owned Kruger Ltd were operating from timber stockpiles after harvesting operations were halted, officials said.
In addition to ground crews, Ontario and Quebec were also using water-bombing aircraft to fight the fires. There were no reports of serious damage to homes in any of the affected regions.
